transcript: Okay, so the first phone that I owned was when I was in year six. It was actually a gift from my godmother for my birthday, and it was a pink, Nokia flip phone. And I'm the, when I first got it, I was so happy because it was my first phone and I could call and text my friends and it was really exciting. Um, and the phone had a call retro design. Um, and And so I loved my phone so much and I used it all the time. And then I remember as the iPhone came out, all of my friends in your six were getting iPhones, which was ridiculous, now that I look back at it. But I remember being so jealous of all my friends who had these grubby, cutting edge iPhones with touch screens. and I had my little cute retro Nokia, but I look back at it and I almost want to have a Nokia again now. I kind of miss my phone because I think it was really nice to be able to focus just on contacting friends and I think that's what phones originally that's what their purpose was so you couldn't contact anyone from anywhere. They're just staying in contact and connected with everyone. And I kind of miss that aspect. I think that phones are very convenient now, but I think there's almost too many things that you can do on a phone.
